questions: With 16 mm footprints at 12 mm spacing, do the sensors overlap enough that the signal saturates or becomes noisy on the tape centre?
Did line_loss_events fall to zero on the slalom and s-bend, and did max_error drop below 0.06 m?
Does steering_oscillation rise with the shorter look-ahead (y = 0.03 m), and does the controller need its kp or sensor_weights rescaled for the larger footprints?
Is the remaining off-track ending driven by turn authority on the tightest bends, and does the oval still show max_error above 0.06 m?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If max_error stays above 0.06 m with line loss at zero, and steering_oscillation is below about 0.25, report the controller signal and kp so I can judge whether turn authority is the limit. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.25, tell me so I can restore y to 0.04 m. If the score is below iteration 0's 96.84, I will revert wheel_track to 0.12 m and mass to 0.6 kg.

intent: Test whether larger sensor footprints and a shorter look-ahead reduce line-loss events and max_error below the 0.06 m off-track floor, with the drivetrain and controller held at iteration 2 values. Changes from iteration 2: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m, and forward sensor row y 0.04 to 0.03 m. Expected result: line_loss_events near zero on all tracks, max_error at or below about 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, and a higher score than iteration 2's 74.95.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the 0.012 m footprint leaves edge sensors reading zero when the robot is at the edge of the tape, so the 0.016 m footprint should reduce line-loss events; (2) the 0.04 m look-ahead adds lag on tight bends, so 0.03 m should reduce max_error on the s-bend and slalom without a large rise in oscillation; (3) wheel_track 0.14 m and mass 0.5 kg were not the cause of the iteration 2 drop, and will be re-tested against iteration 0 once the sensing is fixed. Next race, compare line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation per track against iteration 2.
rationale: Iteration 2 scored 74.95, below iteration 0 (96.84) and iteration 1 (91.28). Every trial on every track still ended off_track, so the score is set by how far the robot strays before it finishes. Max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.064 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track floor, on all three tracks. The floor is fixed by the rule max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4); at body_width 0.18 that is still 0.06 m, so body width cannot help. Widening wheel_track to 0.14 m and lowering mass to 0.5 kg (iteration 2) did not bring max_error below the floor, and slalom line-loss events rose from 1.0 to 1.9. Line loss is still present (1.0 on oval and s-bend, 1.9 on slalom), so the sensing contingency in the Integrator's plan applies: switch to sensor_size 0.016 m with the same seven x positions, so each footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at the edges. Steering oscillation is low (0.18 to 0.20), so the forward row can move closer to the axle, as the Integrator's contingency suggests: y = 0.03 m, which reduces look-ahead lag on the s-bend and slalom where max_error is still above 0.06 m. I keep wheel_track 0.14 m, mass 0.5 kg and kp 7.0 unchanged. The Integrator's controller is tuned to that geometry, so changing it now would confound the result. I change only the two sensing parameters and expect line_loss_events to fall toward zero and max_error to come closer to 0.06 m. If iteration 3 still scores below iteration 0 with these changes, I will revert wheel_track and mass to 0.12 m and 0.6 kg in the next iteration.
